issues.legal_issue: A judge who declines to frame or dilutes a serious charge at the sessions charge stage must give at least brief reasons showing consideration of the material on record.
material_facts: At the charge stage, the judge declined to frame the murder charge and framed a lesser charge, stating only that the case-diary material was insufficient for the more serious charge.
The record included an eyewitness account that the accused struck the deceased on the head and chest, as well as medical evidence supporting that account and linking the injuries to the death.
The order did not discuss that evidence or explain why it did not support the more serious charge; the record disclosed no case of grave and sudden provocation.
issues.conclusion: The order was a bald and inadequate statement that failed to show application of mind to the material. The evidence disclosed a prima facie basis for the more serious charge, and the charge should not have been diluted without adequate reasons.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 227 and 228 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a discharge requires reasons, and the words “after such consideration” in Section 228 connect charge framing to consideration of the record and documents. When a judge drops or dilutes a charge, at least brief reasons must disclose consideration of the material, particularly where a serious charge is involved. At the charge stage, the court asks whether there is ground for presuming the offence, not whether there is sufficient ground for conviction: State of Bihar v. Ramesh Singh, relying on Nirmaljit Singh Hoon v. State of West Bengal and Chandra Deo Singh v. Prokash Chandra Bose. The judge sifts the evidence for the limited purpose of deciding whether the facts emerging from the record constitute the offence: Niranjan Singh v. Jitendra Bhimraj.

rule.if: sessions_charge_proceeding and charge_dropped_or_diluted and (prima_facie_material_supports_serious_charge) and reasons_do_not_show_consideration

predicates.sessions_charge_proceeding: The matter is before a sessions judge at the stage of deciding what charge to frame.
predicates.charge_dropped_or_diluted: The judge declines to frame a more serious charge or substitutes a less serious charge.
predicates.prima_facie_material_supports_serious_ch: The record contains material that, if taken at face value, supports proceeding on the more serious charge.
predicates.reasons_do_not_show_consideration: The order does not explain how the judge considered the material relevant to declining or diluting the charge.

issues.definition: When a sessions judge drops or dilutes a serious charge despite prima facie supporting material, the order must briefly show consideration of that material.

issues.legal_issue: Remarks and corrective suggestions concerning a judicial officer should not be expunged when they are justified by the officer’s demonstrated failure in a judicial decision and are not disparaging.
material_facts: A revisional court found that the judge had inadequately declined to frame the more serious charge despite supporting eyewitness and medical material.
The revisional court described the failure as a blunder and suggested that the High Court administration review the officer’s performance before considering career progression.
The Supreme Court treated the suggestions as corrective and administrative, rather than as disparaging remarks, and found that they were justified by the officer’s failure to discharge his duty.
issues.conclusion: The remarks and suggestions were necessary in the circumstances and were not disparaging; the Court declined to interfere with them.
issues.legal_principle: Superior courts should avoid harsh or disparaging remarks unless they are necessary as an integral part of deciding the case. Such remarks may cause lasting harm to a judicial officer: In the Matter of ‘K’ A Judicial Officer and V.K. Jain v. High Court of Delhi. Remarks are to be removed where they are unnecessary or unjustified, as illustrated by Prakash Singh Teji v. Northern India Goods Transport Company Private Limited. Here, the Court distinguished those cases because the comments were justified corrective suggestions based on the officer’s demonstrated failure and were not disparaging.

predicates.appeal_challenging_remarks_about_judicia: The proceeding is an appeal seeking removal of remarks made about a judicial officer in a superior court’s order.
predicates.remarks_based_on_demonstrated_judicial_f: The remarks rest on a judicial error or failure established from the record before the superior court.
predicates.remarks_are_corrective_not_disparaging: The comments serve a corrective or administrative purpose and do not amount to unjustified disparagement.

issues.definition: Remarks about a judicial officer remain when an appeal challenges them, they are grounded in a demonstrated judicial failure, and they are corrective rather than disparaging.

issues.legal_issue: A judicial officer has no automatic entitlement to a selection grade, and the administration may withhold it after reviewing the officer’s record and identifying serious deficiencies.
material_facts: Following the revisional court’s suggestion, the High Court administration reviewed the officer’s record and denied him the selection grade.
The Supreme Court noted the officer’s failure to discharge his duty in framing the charge and deficiencies in his service record.
The officer challenged the revisional court’s observations that led to the review, rather than directly challenging the denial of the selection grade.
issues.conclusion: The selection grade was not a matter of right, and the Court found no reason to interfere with the administration’s review and resulting denial of the grade.
issues.legal_principle: A selection grade is not conferred as a matter of right; the concerned officer’s record is to be considered. The Court held that the High Court administration had reviewed the record and acted on the serious deficiencies it identified. No earlier case was relied on for this proposition.

predicates.service_grade_review: The matter concerns an administrative decision on whether a judicial officer should receive a higher service grade.
predicates.service_record_reviewed: The administration examines the officer’s service record before deciding whether to grant the grade.
predicates.serious_performance_deficiencies_found: The review identifies serious deficiencies in the officer’s performance or service record.

issues.definition: A higher service grade may be withheld when the administration reviews the officer’s record and finds serious performance deficiencies.
